Invariants — hold at every read, under concurrency and retries - **R-1-001** The sum of all wallet balances always equals the sum of the `balance` values seeded by the last successful `POST /_test/reset` (or restored by `POST /_test/import`), at every read, after any mix of concurrent payments, request payments, splits, settlements and replays. (§1.1, §9) [invariant] - **R-1-002** No wallet balance is ever negative, not even transiently: no observable read and no intermediate state inside any operation leaves a balance below zero. (§1.2) [invariant] - **R-1-003** A payment request moves money at most once: a replayed write returns the original response and makes no further state change. (§1.3, §7) [invariant] - **R-1-004** Every amount in the API and in storage is an exact integer count of minor units; no floating-point rounding error is ever observable, and split shares sum exactly to the split `amount`. (§4, §9) [invariant] - **R-1-005** No request produces a 5xx response, including under 50 concurrent in-flight requests. (§5) [invariant] - **R-1-006** Concurrent requests produce results equal to executing them one at a time in some order (serializable); the debit and credit of a payment are one atomic step, never visible in one wallet and not the other, and a failed payment leaves no trace in either wallet. (§8) [invariant] - **R-1-007** A rejected write (any 4xx) changes no balance, creates no payment, no request and no settlement, and leaves no record other than those the idempotency rules require. (§5, §7, §11) [invariant] ## B. Delivery and deployment - **R-1-010** The stage folder contains a `Dockerfile` that builds the service with no manual setup, and a `RUN.md` giving the exact build-and-start command. (§2) - **R-1-011** The image runs standalone with `-e PORT=<port>` and a port mapping; no compose file, external service, volume or sidecar is needed to start or serve. (§2) - **R-1-012** The service listens on `0.0.0.0` on the port given by the `PORT` environment variable, defaulting to `8080` when `PORT` is unset. (§3.1) - **R-1-013** The container makes no outbound network request at run time; all dependencies, fonts, scripts, stylesheets and seed data are baked into the image during build. (§2) - **R-1-014** `GET /health` returns `200` with body `{"status": "ok"}` once the service and its data store can serve requests, within 60 s of container start. Non-200 before readiness is permitted. (§3.2) - **R-1-015** The service stays correct and responsive within 2 vCPU and 2 GiB with up to 50 requests in flight; every request other than the test-control endpoints completes within 5 s, and `POST /_test/reset`, `POST /_test/import` and `GET /_test/export` within 10 s. (§2, §10) [limit] - **R-1-016** Service state need not survive a container restart; no on-disk durability is required. (§2) ## C. Conventions - **R-1-020** Every JSON response carries `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`, and request bodies are read as UTF-8 JSON. (§3.4) - **R-1-021** Every timestamp in a response is RFC 3339 with an explicit offset (e.g. `2026-09-24T19:00:00+00:00`); a bare local time or a naive offset-less form is never emitted. (§3.4) - **R-1-022** Unknown fields in any request body are ignored and are never an error. (§3.4) - **R-1-023** Unknown query parameters on any endpoint are ignored and are never an error. (§3.4) - **R-1-024** Every id the service assigns is an opaque string of at most 64 characters; format is the implementation's choice but ids are unique within their kind for the life of a reset. (§3.4) - **R-1-025** Seeded ids supplied in a fixture are used verbatim as the service's ids for those users, payments and requests, and are returned unchanged by the API. (§4) ## D. Model: currency, users, handles - **R-1-030** The service has exactly one currency and one `minor_units` value, both declared by the fixture; `minor_units` is `0`, `2` or `3`, and fixtures use `EUR` (2), `JPY` (0) and `BHD` (3). (§4) - **R-1-031** Every API `amount` is an integer count of minor units; JSON `1000`, `1000.0` and `1e3` are all accepted as the same valid amount because their numeric value is integral. (§4) - **R-1-032** A JSON boolean or string in an `amount` field is not a number and is rejected with `422 validation_failed` (not `400`). (§4, §5) - **R-1-033** A numeric `amount` with a non-integral value (e.g. `10.5`, `1e-1`) is `422 validation_failed`. (§8) - **R-1-034** Every user has a handle that is unique across the service, matches `^[a-z0-9_]{1,20}$`, and never changes once set. (§4) - **R-1-035** Recipients and payers are identified in request bodies by handle only; no directory or user-search endpoint exists. (§4) - **R-1-036** A user created through `POST /auth/signup` gets a handle derived from the email: take the local part (everything before the first `@`), lowercase it, replace every character outside `[a-z0-9_]` with `_`, then truncate to 20 characters. (§4, §6) - **R-1-037** A newly signed-up user starts with balance `0`, can immediately receive money and can immediately be asked for money. (§4) ## E. Fixture, reset, and seeding - **R-1-040** `POST /_test/reset` with a fixture body replaces **all** service state and returns `204 No Content`; after it returns, every subsequent request sees only that fixture and nothing from before it. (§3.3) - **R-1-041** `POST /_test/reset` requires no authentication, is enabled in the delivered image, and may be called repeatedly; each call fully replaces the previous state. (§3.3) - **R-1-042** A reset fixture seeds `currency`, `minor_units`, `users` (`id`, `email`, `password`, `display_name`, `handle`, `balance`), optional `payments` (`id`, `from_user_id`, `to_user_id`, `amount`, `note`, `visibility`), optional `requests` (`id`, `requester_id`, `payer_id`, `amount`, `note`, `status`) and optional `settlement_operator_ids` (default `[]`). (§4, §11) - **R-1-043** A seeded user's `balance` is the wallet balance **after** every seeded payment; seeded payments are **not** replayed against balances, so loading them leaves the seeded balance unchanged. (§4) - **R-1-044** Seeded users can log in with the seeded plaintext `password` immediately after reset. (§4) - **R-1-045** A fixture containing any `balance` below zero makes `POST /_test/reset` return `422 validation_failed` and change nothing (the prior state remains fully intact and servable). (§4) - **R-1-046** A reset body that does not parse as JSON, or whose top level is not a JSON object, is `400 malformed_request` and changes nothing. (§5) - **R-1-047** A fixture that is structurally unusable — a missing required user field, a duplicate user `id` or `handle`, a `handle` not matching `^[a-z0-9_]{1,20}$`, a `minor_units` outside `{0,2,3}`, a payment or request referencing an unknown user id, or a seeded `status` outside the four request statuses — is `422 validation_failed` and changes nothing. (§4, §5) - **R-1-048** Any field the fixture does not mention is ignored, and a fixture omitting `payments`, `requests` or `settlement_operator_ids` is valid; the omitted collection is empty. (§3.4, §4, §11) - **R-1-049** Seeded requests keep their seeded `status`; a seeded non-`pending` request is not payable and a seeded `pending` request is payable exactly like an API-created one. (§4, §8) - **R-1-050** There is no administrative balance endpoint, and no endpoint other than reset/import may set a balance directly. (§4) ## F. Errors and precedence - **R-1-060** Every 4xx and 5xx response body is exactly `{"error": {"code": "<code>", "message": "<any wording>"}}` with the specified status and code; `message` wording is free but must be a non-empty string. (§5) - **R-1-061** `400 malformed_request`: the body does not parse as JSON, the top level is not a JSON object, or a field is of the wrong JSON type and no endpoint-specific rule overrides it. `message` wording is free but must be a non-empty string. - **R-1-061** `400 malformed_request`: the body does not parse as JSON, the top level is not a JSON object, or a field is of the wrong JSON type and no endpoint-specific rule overrides it. - **R-1-062** `400 missing_idempotency_key`: a required `Idempotency-Key` header is absent or empty. - **R-1-063** `401 unauthenticated`: the `Authorization` header is missing, not of the form `Bearer <token>`, or carries an unknown token. - **R-1-064** `403 forbidden`: the caller is authenticated but not permitted to act on this resource. - **R-1-065** `404 not_found`: no such resource, or the resource is not visible to this caller. - **R-1-066** `409 idempotency_key_reuse`: the key was already used by this caller with a different request body on the same method and path. - **R-1-067** `422 validation_failed`: a required field or query parameter is missing, or a stated rule is violated and no more specific code applies. - **R-1-068** A field of the **correct** JSON type with an invalid format or out-of-range value is `422 validation_failed` unless the endpoint names a different code; omitting a required field is `422 validation_failed`. - **R-1-071** An integer-valued **query parameter** must be written as plain decimal digits; `1e9`, `4.0`, `+4`, ` 4`, `0x4` and an empty value are `422 validation_failed` whatever their numeric value. Whatever you choose: **validate the whole precedence chain before you take the write lock, and do check-and-apply for funds inside it** — a funds check outside the lock passes every spec test and fails the storm. Never use a float for money anywhere, including JSON serialization (if your language's JSON encoder can emit `1000.0` for an integer, assert against that). **Delivery and deployment** - **R-1-010** The stage folder contains a `Dockerfile` that builds the service with no manual setup, and a `RUN.md` giving the exact build-and-start command. - **R-1-011** The image runs standalone with `-e PORT=<port>` and a port mapping; no compose file, external service, volume or sidecar is needed to start or serve. - **R-1-012** The service listens on `0.0.0.0` on the port given by the `PORT` environment variable, defaulting to `8080` when `PORT` is unset. - **R-1-013** The container makes no outbound network request at run time; all dependencies, fonts, scripts, stylesheets and seed data are baked into the image during build. - **R-1-014** `GET /health` returns `200` with body `{"status": "ok"}` once the service and its data store can serve requests, within 60 s of container start. Non-200 before readiness is permitted. - **R-1-015** The service stays correct and responsive within 2 vCPU and 2 GiB with up to 50 requests in flight; every request other than the test-control endpoints completes within 5 s, and `POST /_test/reset`, `POST /_test/import` and `GET /_test/export` within 10 s. - **R-1-016** Service state need not survive a container restart; no on-disk durability is required. **Conventions** - **R-1-020** Every JSON response carries `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`, and request bodies are read as UTF-8 JSON. - **R-1-021** Every timestamp in a response is RFC 3339 with an explicit offset (e.g. `2026-09-24T19:00:00+00:00`); a bare local time or a naive offset-less form is never emitted. - **R-1-022** Unknown fields in any request body are ignored and are never an error. - **R-1-023** Unknown query parameters on any endpoint are ignored and are never an error. - **R-1-024** Every id the service assigns is an opaque string of at most 64 characters; format is the implementation's choice but ids are unique within their kind for the life of a reset. - **R-1-025** Seeded ids supplied in a fixture are used verbatim as the service's ids for those users, payments and requests, and are returned unchanged by the API. **Errors and precedence — the core of this item** - **R-1-060** Every 4xx and 5xx response body is exactly `{"error": {"code": "<code>", "message": "<any wording>"}}` with the specified status and code; `message` wording is free but must be a non-empty string. - **R-1-061** `400 malformed_request`: the body does not parse as JSON, the top level is not a JSON object, or a field is of the wrong JSON type and no endpoint-specific rule overrides it. - **R-1-062** `400 missing_idempotency_key`: a required `Idempotency-Key` header is absent or empty. - **R-1-063** `401 unauthenticated`: the `Authorization` header is missing, not of the form `Bearer <token>`, or carries an unknown token. - **R-1-064** `403 forbidden`: the caller is authenticated but not permitted to act on this resource. - **R-1-065** `404 not_found`: no such resource, or the resource is not visible to this caller. - **R-1-066** `409 idempotency_key_reuse`: the key was already used by this caller with a different request body on the same method and path. - **R-1-067** `422 validation_failed`: a required field or query parameter is missing, or a stated rule is violated and no more specific code applies. - **R-1-068** A field of the **correct** JSON type with an invalid format or out-of-range value is `422 validation_failed` unless the endpoint names a different code; this covers invalid instants, negative counts and values over a stated maximum or length. - **R-1-069** Endpoint field rules take precedence over the wrong-type rule for three fields: an invalid `amount` (including a string or boolean), a non-string `note` (including `null`), and any `visibility` other than `"public"` or `"private"` are all `422 validation_failed`, never `400`. - **R-1-070** Omitting an optional field selects its default and is never an error; omitting a required field is `422 validation_failed`. - **R-1-071** An integer-valued **query parameter** must be written as plain decimal digits; `1e9`, `4.0`, `+4`, ` 4`, `0x4` and an empty value are `422 validation_failed` whatever their numeric value. A leading `-` is only valid where negative values are. - **R-1-072** `Idempotency-Key` must be 1 to 255 characters: longer than 255 is `422 validation_failed`; absent or empty is `400 missing_idempotency_key`. - **R-1-073** `limit` is an integer 1 to 200; anything else (including `0`, `201`, negative or non-digit forms) is `422 validation_failed`. - **R-1-074** `offset` is an integer 0 or more; anything else is `422 validation_failed`. - **R-1-075** **PLANNER DECISION — implement exactly this chain, once, shared by every endpoint.** Error precedence is, in order: (1) `401 unauthenticated`; (2) endpoint-level permission not depending on the body (`403 forbidden` for a non-operator on `POST /settlements`); (3) `400 malformed_request` for an unparseable or non-object body; (4) `400 missing_idempotency_key`; (5) `422 validation_failed` for an over-long `Idempotency-Key`; (6) idempotency resolution (`200` replay or `409 idempotency_key_reuse`); (7) endpoint field validation (`422`, including `self_payment` / `self_request`); (8) resource lookup (`404 not_found`); (9) permission on the looked-up resource (`403 forbidden`); (10) resource-state checks (`409 request_not_pending`); (11) funds (`409 insufficient_funds`). - **R-1-076** **PLANNER DECISION.** Within step (7), body fields are validated in this fixed order so the returned code is deterministic: required-field presence → wrong-type fields → `amount` range and integrality → `note` length → `visibility` value → handle syntax → duplicate/empty collection rules → self-reference (`self_payment` / `self_request`). - **R-1-077** **PLANNER DECISION.** A `to_handle`, `payer_handle` or participant handle that is a string but does not match `^[a-z0-9_]{1,20}$` is `422 validation_failed`; a syntactically valid handle with no such user is `404 not_found`. A non-string handle is `400 malformed_request`. - **R-1-078** A 4xx response never leaks a resource the caller may not see: a request or payment the caller is not party to is reported with the same code and body as a nonexistent one, except where the spec names `403 forbidden`. **Amount parsing, needed by the engine now and used by every write later** - **R-1-031** Every API `amount` is an integer count of minor units; JSON `1000`, `1000.0` and `1e3` are all accepted as the same valid amount because their numeric value is integral. - **R-1-032** A JSON boolean or string in an `amount` field is not a number and is rejected with `422 validation_failed` (not `400`). - **R-1-033** A numeric `amount` with a non-integral value (e.g. `10.5`, `1e-1`) is `422 validation_failed`. ## Handoff when you are done Commit only the files you authored (`git add <paths>`, never `git add -A`), as `git commit --author "Builder <builder@band.local>"`. No other endpoint requires or honours one. - **R-1-101** Idempotency state is scoped to the authenticated **user**: two different users may use the same key string on the same path with no interaction. - **R-1-102** A replay is the same user sending the same method, the same path **and** the same body. The same key with the same body on a **different path** is a different request and must succeed normally. - **R-1-103** First use of a key returns the endpoint's normal success status, `201`. - **R-1-104** A replay returns `200` with a body identical to the original response **as a JSON value**. - **R-1-105** The same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_key_reuse` and changes nothing. - **R-1-106** "Same body" is the same JSON value after parsing: key order and whitespace do not matter. **Numbers compare by exact numeric value**, so `1000`, `1000.0` and `1e3` in the same field *are* the same body. An **absent** key versus that key **present with its default value** are **different** bodies — so `{}` and `{"visibility":"public"}` are different, and reusing one key across them is `409 idempotency_key_reuse`. - **R-1-107** A key reused after the original request failed with **any** 4xx is treated as a first use and may succeed. - **R-1-108** For N concurrent identical requests with an unused key, **exactly one** returns `201` and the rest return `200` with the identical body. The operation takes effect exactly once. - **R-1-109** A successful replay returns the original response even after the underlying resource has changed, been paid, declined or cancelled, and makes no further state change. - **R-1-110** Once the body has parsed as a JSON object and the caller is authenticated, a claimed key is resolved **before** endpoint field validation and before any current-resource check. So replaying a successful key with an invalid body still returns `409 idempotency_key_reuse`, and replaying a successful `pay` returns `200` rather than `409 request_not_pending`. - **R-1-111** A claimed key's stored record keeps the request body, the response status and the full response body, and survives export/import (R-1-206). - **R-1-112** A replay returns the stored response body **verbatim**; it is never re-rendered from the current resource. A replay of a key claimed under an earlier stage's schema returns exactly that earlier body, without any field a later stage added to the resource (no `authorization_id`, no `refund_of`). This is what makes R-1-104 and R-1-206 hold across an upgrade. - **R-1-072** `Idempotency-Key` 1..255 characters: over 255 is `422 validation_failed`; absent or empty is `400 missing_idempotency_key`. - **R-1-075** steps (4)(5)(6): missing key → key length → idempotency resolution, all **before** field validation, lookup, resource permission, state and funds. ## The hard parts — work these out explicitly **R-1-108 is the one that bites.** A losing racer must **not** get `409`, and must not get an error: it has to end up returning `200` with the winner's stored body. Three states, not two — a key is *unclaimed*, *in flight*, or *complete*. A racer that finds the key in flight must wait for the winner to finish and then return its stored response. If you implement "claim or 409" you will pass every sequential test and fail the storm, which sends 300 replays at 50-way concurrency. Claim the key and run the operation under the **same** serialization point you already use for funds, so "in flight" is never observable as a gap. **R-1-112 vs R-1-104 is a trap for later stages.** Store the serialized response body at the moment you produce it and return those bytes (or that exact parsed value) on replay. Do **not** store a reference to the payment and re-render it — that would silently add stage-2's `authorization_id` and stage-4's `refund_of` to replays of stage-1 keys and break gate 5's upgrade check. @prashant101007/redline's hook fingerprints exactly this. **R-1-107 interacts with R-1-108.** If the winner's operation ends in a 4xx, the key must be released, not left claimed — otherwise a later legitimate retry gets a stale `409` or hangs. Make the claim transactional with the outcome: commit the record only on success, release on 4xx. **Derived cases no example shows** — I expect these to be probed: 1. Key scoping is (user, method, path, key) — not (user, key). Same key, same body, different path → both succeed (R-1-102). Same key on `POST /payments` and `POST /requests` are unrelated records. 2. Path identity for parameterised paths is the **concrete** path: `POST /requests/rq_1/pay` and `POST /requests/rq_2/pay` with the same key and the same body `{}` are different paths, so both succeed. 3. Two users, same key string, same path, different bodies → both `201`, no interference (R-1-101). 4. `409 idempotency_key_reuse` must not consume or alter the original record: after it, replaying the *original* body still returns `200` with the original response. 5. A replay must return `200` even when the original returned `201` — the status differs, the body does not. 6. Body equality must ignore key order *recursively*, including inside `transfers` entries and `participant_handles` — but **array order is significant** (`["ada","bob"]` ≠ `["bob","ada"]`, and they genuinely produce different splits). 7. Unknown fields are ignored for *validation* (R-1-022) but they are part of the **body** for equality: `{"amount":1}` and `{"amount":1,"zz":2}` are different JSON values, so the same key across them is `409`. Do not strip unknown fields before hashing. 8. An over-255-character key is `422` and claims nothing, so the same (shortened) key is still unused afterwards. 9. A key whose original request 4xx'd is reusable even with a *different* body (R-1-107 — it was never claimed). 10. `POST /requests/{id}/decline` and `/cancel` take **no** key (R-1-100): sending `Idempotency-Key` on them is ignored, never an error, and never stored. ## Handoff Commit with the pathspec form; `git status --porcelain` first. If they are absent, `shares` has `n` entries and `requests` has `n`; if present, `shares` has `n` and `requests` has `n-1`. The body was then written in a **separate** `wfile.write()` call right after — two writes, two candidate TCP segments. `test_http_framing.py`'s `_send_raw` helper stops reading as soon as it sees `\r\n\r\n` anywhere in the accumulated bytes, not once it's read the declared `Content-Length` of body — so if the OS/scheduler split the two writes across segments, the test (and, more importantly, anything else watching for "response complete" the same cheap way) could see a complete, correct status line and headers with no body, even though the server sent everything correctly and in order. Fixed with `_end_headers_with_body()`: appends the blank-line terminator and the body to the **same** `_headers_buffer` the stdlib already accumulates headers into, then issues **one** `wfile.write()` for the whole response. Replaces `end_headers()` + a trailing body write in `send_error`, `_write_json`, and `do_OPTIONS` — every response path now writes in one shot. The drain-before-close fix from `c552f89` stays; it's a separate, still-real risk (RST discarding an already-sent response when unread input remains on close) and the two fixes are complementary. ## The 50-iteration evidence, against the real fix Started the actual service as a separate process, ran both relevant tests 50 times each via direct subprocess calls to pytest: - `test_over_long_header_block_400`: **50/50 passed, zero failures** - `test_over_long_request_line_400`: **50/50 passed, zero failures** ## Gate 2, once, with `--commit` ``` .venv/bin/python -m factory.gates.run stage-1 --gates 2 --commit 639e71a ``` **314 passed, 0 failed** — exactly as expected.

Corrections - **R-3-050** `POST /payments/{payment_id}/corrections` requires an `Idempotency-Key` and the **original sender**. It is the eighth idempotent write path. - **R-3-051** An authenticated non-sender is `403 forbidden`; an unknown payment is `404 not_found`; no token is `401 unauthenticated`. - **R-3-052** The body is `{"expected_revision", "amount", "effective_at", "reason"}` and **all four fields are required**; omitting any is `422 validation_failed`. - **R-3-053** `expected_revision` is a positive integer; `amount` is an integer `0..1000000000` (zero reverses the entire payment); `reason` is a string of 1..200 characters; `effective_at` is an RFC 3339 instant **not later than now**. [invariant] - **R-3-068** **PLANNER DECISION.** Correction error precedence, extending R-1-075: `401` → `404 not_found` (unknown payment) → `403 forbidden` (non-sender) → `400 missing_idempotency_key` → idempotency resolution → `422 validation_failed` (field rules) → `422 linked_payment_immutable` → `409 stale_revision` → `409 insufficient_funds` → `409 historical_overdraft`.
